<!--
  Thanks for submitting a pull request!
  We appreciate you spending the time to work on these changes. Please provide enough information so that others can review your pull request. The three fields below are mandatory.

  Before submitting a pull request, please make sure the following is done:

  1. Fork [the repository](https://github.com/facebook/react) and create your branch from `master`.
  2. Run `yarn` in the repository root.
  3. If you've fixed a bug or added code that should be tested, add tests!
  4. Ensure the test suite passes (`yarn test`). Tip: `yarn test --watch TestName` is helpful in development.
  5. Run `yarn test --prod` to test in the production environment. It supports the same options as `yarn test`.
  6. If you need a debugger, run `yarn debug-test --watch TestName`, open `chrome://inspect`, and press "Inspect".
  7. Format your code with [prettier](https://github.com/prettier/prettier) (`yarn prettier`).
  8. Make sure your code lints (`yarn lint`). Tip: `yarn linc` to only check changed files.
  9. Run the [Flow](https://flowtype.org/) type checks (`yarn flow`).
  10. If you haven't already, complete the CLA.

  Learn more about contributing: https://reactjs.org/docs/how-to-contribute.html
-->

## Summary

<!-- Explain the **motivation** for making this change. What existing problem does the pull request solve? -->
Fixes #20204.

Dependency array parsing crashes when it encounters optional-chained function calls, e.g. `props?.attribute.method()`.

Given:
```js
useEffect(() => {}, [someObject?.optionalField.method()]);
```

Expected:
- `React Hook useEffect has a complex expression in the dependency array. Extract it to a separate variable so it can be statically checked.`

Actual: 
- `Cannot read property 'type' of undefined`
- No lint errors are displayed due to linter crash


## Test Plan

<!-- Demonstrate the code is solid. Example: The exact commands you ran and their output, screenshots / videos if the pull request changes the user interface. -->
Unit tests:
- Added missing test for checking function call as dependency: `[props.method()]`
- Added test validating fix. Contains optional-chained function call: `[props?.attribute.method()]`

Regression:
- Linted [164 repositories](https://github.com/AriPerkkio/eslint-remote-tester/blob/master/eslint-remote-tester.react.config.js#L2-L168) before and after the fix. The only change was that the previously crashing file was no more crashing. Every other lint warning was as before.

issue.body:
<!--
    ESLint adheres to the Open JS Foundation Code of Conduct:
    https://eslint.org/conduct

    This template is for requesting a change that is not a bug fix, rule change, or new rule. If you are here for another reason, please see below:

    1. To report a bug: https://eslint.org/docs/developer-guide/contributing/reporting-bugs
    2. To request a rule change: https://eslint.org/docs/developer-guide/contributing/rule-changes
    3. To propose a new rule: https://eslint.org/docs/developer-guide/contributing/new-rules
    4. If you have any questions, please stop by our chatroom: https://eslint.org/chat

    Note that leaving sections blank will make it difficult for us to troubleshoot and we may have to close the issue.
-->

**The version of ESLint you are using.**

`ESLint: 7.12.1`

**The problem you want to solve.**

Error handling of crashing rules could be improved. By a "crashing rule" I mean a case where ESLint rule throws an error instead of using the `context.report` API. These issues are often caused by unsafe accessing of a node property, e.g. `node.callee.name` -> `Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read property 'name' of undefined`. I've noticed that these are quite common in various ESlint plugins.

Current functionality when erroneous rule causes linter to crash:
1. Cause of the crash is not clear. Users have to study the stack trace in order to figure out which rule caused the crash.
2. Every other valid linting problems are lost. If rule A is reporting valid linting problem, it is not visible due to rule B causing linter crash.

Let's use real-world example from `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`, [Bug: eslint-plugin-react-hooks: Cannot read property 'type' of undefined at analyzePropertyChain #20204](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/20204).

<details>
    <summary>Current behavior</summary>

ESLint error message does not indicate which rule caused the crash.

```bash
$ node ./node_modules/.bin/eslint ./lib


Oops! Something went wrong! :(

ESLint: 7.12.1

TypeError: Cannot read property 'type' of undefined
Occurred while linting /<root-path-removed>/eslint-remote-tester/lib/ui/hooks/useOnExit.ts:5
    at analyzePropertyChain (/<root-path-removed>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint-plugin-react-hooks/cjs/eslint-plugin-react-hooks.development.js:2235:12)
    at analyzePropertyChain (/<root-path-removed>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint-plugin-react-hooks/cjs/eslint-plugin-react-hooks.development.js:2264:20)
    at /<root-path-removed>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint-plugin-react-hooks/cjs/eslint-plugin-react-hooks.development.js:1297:34
    at Array.forEach (<anonymous>)
    at visitFunctionWithDependencies (/<root-path-removed>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint-plugin-react-hooks/cjs/eslint-plugin-react-hooks.development.js:1277:43)
    at visitCallExpression (/<root-path-removed>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint-plugin-react-hooks/cjs/eslint-plugin-react-hooks.development.js:1737:11)
    at /<root-path-removed>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint/lib/linter/safe-emitter.js:49:25
    at Array.forEach (<anonymous>)
    at Object.emit (/<root-path-removed>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint/lib/linter/safe-emitter.js:47:38)
    at NodeEventGenerator.applySelector (/<root-path-removed>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint/lib/linter/node-event-generator.js:254:26)
```

Every other valid linting error is lost:

![eslint-crash-current-behavior](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14806298/99876710-1858e300-2c01-11eb-9e96-2d3b40bd3c7a.png)

</details>


By fixing the first issue users would know what rule caused the issue. After figuring out how ESlint runs the rules I created a POC for this fix.

<details>
    <summary>Crashing rule included in the error message</summary>

```bash
$ node ./node_modules/.bin/eslint ./lib


Oops! Something went wrong! :(

ESLint: 7.12.1

TypeError: Cannot read property 'type' of undefined caused by rule "react-hooks/exhaustive-deps"
Occurred while linting /<removed-root-path>/eslint-remote-tester/lib/ui/hooks/useOnExit.ts:5
    at /<removed-root-path>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint/lib/linter/safe-emitter.js:54:31
    at Array.forEach (<anonymous>)
    at Object.emit (/<removed-root-path>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint/lib/linter/safe-emitter.js:47:38)
    at NodeEventGenerator.applySelector (/<removed-root-path>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint/lib/linter/node-event-generator.js:254:26)
    at NodeEventGenerator.applySelectors (/<removed-root-path>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint/lib/linter/node-event-generator.js:283:22)
    at NodeEventGenerator.enterNode (/<removed-root-path>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint/lib/linter/node-event-generator.js:297:14)
    at CodePathAnalyzer.enterNode (/<removed-root-path>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint/lib/linter/code-path-analysis/code-path-analyzer.js:711:23)
    at /<removed-root-path>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint/lib/linter/linter.js:966:32
    at Array.forEach (<anonymous>)
    at runRules (/<removed-root-path>/eslint-remote-tester/node_modules/eslint/lib/linter/linter.js:961:15)
```

However every other valid linting error is still lost:
![eslint-crash-rule-included](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14806298/99876719-2b6bb300-2c01-11eb-9815-5cdc4373a519.png)

</details>

By fixing the second issue users would still be able to see valid linting errors. Instead of throwing an Error from `linter.js` it could parse `safe-emitter.js`'s error and report it via `context.report`. I'm not sure whether this is against principles of ESlint but this would surely improve user experience.

<details>
    <summary>Crashing rule reported via `context.report`</summary>

These examples also contain fix for the first issue.

Other linting errors are not lost:
```bash
$ node ./node_modules/.bin/eslint ./lib

/<removed-rooth-path>/eslint-remote-tester/lib/ui/hooks/useOnExit.ts
  5:5   warning  Cannot read property 'type' of undefined caused by rule "react-hooks/exhaustive-deps"  react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  8:11  warning  'id' is assigned a value but never used                                                @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars

✖ 2 problems (0 errors, 2 warnings)
```
![eslint-crash-reported](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/14806298/99876726-345c8480-2c01-11eb-8329-d8eb8b5166bd.png)

</details>

**Your take on the correct solution to problem.**

I would like to see the first issue (include rule name in error message) fixed. The second is not that clear and requires discussion.

**Are you willing to submit a pull request to implement this change?**
Yes! The POCs above are working OK in my local environment. Before I go any further with the implementation I would like to hear opinnions from the maintainers. The main goal here is to improve user and development experience of ESlint and its community plugins.
